title: Quality-Aware Quantization Rollout PRD
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:

This PRD defines a product-led rollout for model quantization profiles that reduces per-token inference cost while enforcing measurable quality guardrails across Redwood’s Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment surfaces. The goal is a staged release that enables customers to opt-in to quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) with predictable latency, throughput, and worst-case quality bounds, and packaging and pricing options that reflect the economics and risk profile.

Why this matters:
- Quantization is the single highest-impact operational lever to reduce GPU memory footprint and per-token cost for many open models.
- Uncontrolled quantization introduces quality regressions that manifest differently per workload and prompt distribution.
- Customers (especially enterprise/Dedicated/Private) need predictable, measurable guarantees and a simple opt-in/rollback experience.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: definition of quantization profile taxonomy, acceptance metrics, rollout strategy (canary → staged → general), packaging/pricing options, telemetry & alerting requirements, owner and runbook for rollback.
- Out of scope: model training changes, new quantization algorithm R&D (research can be referenced but not implemented as part of this rollout), deep kernel-level optimization beyond selected runtime knobs (handled by eng-serving-runtime ongoing work).

Product overview and definitions:
- Quantization profile: a named bundle of model artifact + runtime flags + config that produce a deterministic inference variant (e.g., q4_legacy, q4_higher_bias, q8_dynamic).
- Quality guardrail: a set of automated checks (metric thresholds and delta budgets) that must be met before a variant advances stages. Examples: Perplexity delta vs baseline, BLEU/ROUGE regressions on prompt-sets, hallucination rate on safety prompts, human accept rate on sample prompts.
- Packaging tier types: 1) Hosted opt-in (per-account toggle + usage reporting), 2) Dedicated default (tenant-level policy selectable with SLA caveats), 3) Private reference package (deployment artifacts + guidance, no managed fallback).

Requirements (customer-facing):
1) Opt-in experience: customers can enable quantized variants for a specific model version via API flag and Console toggle. Change must be reversible for individual keys.
2) Transparency: list the quantization profile, estimated per-token cost delta, expected latency changes, and known failure modes in the Console and API metadata.
3) Safety/Quality SLO: no more than 2% customer-visible quality regressions (measured by configured evals) vs baseline for Hosted opt-in; Dedicated customers can select a tighter 1% SLA in their contract.
4) Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to a compatible non-quantized variant on an exceeded error or latency threshold.
5) Billing: quantization-driven unit pricing reflected in invoices and quotas with clear conversion rates.

Product requirements (internal):
- PR-1: Profile Registry: central store (service: model-registry) of quantization profiles, metadata, and compatibility matrix. Fields: profile_name, model_arch, quant_bits, expected_memory, validated_on_prompt_set_ids.
- PR-2: Telemetry hooks: add telemetry events for profile selection, per-request profile_id, quality-check outcomes, and fallback triggers.
- PR-3: Eval suite integration: every profile must be validated against a standard prompt-set (quality-guardrails collection) with automated daily replays and statistical drift alerts.
- PR-4: Rollout control plane: support staged flags per-customer and global canary cohorts with percent rollouts and time windows.
- PR-5: Billing mapping: define pricing multiplier table and ensure metering emits tokens_consumed_{profile_name} dimension.

Acceptance criteria and metrics (quantitative):
- Quality: For each profile, measured automated eval delta (primary metric = normalized utility score) must be <=1.5% for Hosted canary to move to general availability; dedicated SLA target configurable to 1%.
- Latency: P50 token generation latency must not increase by more than 20% vs baseline for small-sequence workloads; p99 must remain under configured tenant SLO (default 2s).
- Cost: Expected per-token cost reduction >= 20% for q4 profiles vs baseline; billing accuracy <0.5% error on metering.
- Reliability: Fallback success rate > 99.95% when triggered; no cascading failures across tenants.

Design overview (high level):
1) Profile registry + metadata surfaced in model-catalog UI.
2) Evaluation pipeline: nightly replay job that runs new commits and profiles against canonical prompt-sets and pushes metrics to Optimize dashboards.
3) Runtime tagging: inference requests carry profile_id; the serving runtime selects corresponding kernels and memory layouts.
4) Canary orchestration: use rollout service to target 1% external traffic cohort, monitor real-time metrics and automated quality checks.
5) Billing plumbing: augment metering job to annotate tokens by profile and include in per-key usage exports.

Detailed rollout plan (phases):
Phase 0 - Preparation (2–4 weeks):
- Implement Profile Registry and Console UI mockups.
- Create canonical prompt-sets (safety, hallucination, domain-specific) and register them.
- Define billing multipliers and update billing schema.
- Owners: Product (Maya Chen), Runtime (Rafael Ortega), Billing (Priya Desai).

Phase 1 - Internal Canary (2 weeks):
- Enable profiles for internal teams and Redwood QA. Run daily automated evals; collect human raters for 500 sample prompts.
- Stop criteria: any automated metric exceeding threshold or >0.5% human regression.

Phase 2 - External Controlled Canary (4 weeks):
- Target 1% of traffic for hosted public accounts and a small cohort of Dedicated customers (opt-in). Monitor daily: utility score, latency, fallback rate, metering.
- Accept criteria: quality <=1.5% delta, latency p50 within 20%, billing annotations validated.

Phase 3 - Staged Expansion (6–8 weeks):
- Expand to 10% → 50% cohorts with progressive checks. For Dedicated customers signed to tighter SLAs, require explicit contract flag before expansion.

Phase 4 - GA and Packaging (2 weeks):
- Mark profiles as GA in Catalog. Publish pricing multipliers and Console toggles. Update docs and release notes.

Rollback and mitigation playbook (short):
1) Automatic rollback: if automated quality checks breach thresholds for more than 3 consecutive windows, the control plane will revert affected requests to baseline model and notify SRE/PD.
2) Manual rollback: product or runtime can instantly flip tenant toggles; billing records preserved.
3) Post-incident triage: collect saved generations, telemetry, and prompt-set failures for regression triage.

Telemetry and alerting requirements:
- Dashboards: per-profile KPI dashboards (quality delta, p50/p90/p99 latency, fallback rate, billing delta).
- Alerts: threshold alerts for quality delta > configured (default 1.5%), fallback rate spikes >0.5% absolute, metering mismatch >0.5% daily.
- Logging: sample-level logging for failed checks with redaction rules; store sample artifacts to a secure bucket for triage.

Packaging and pricing considerations:
- Hosted: default opt-in with a visible per-token discount; usage shows both baseline and quantized token counts.
- Dedicated: offer two tiers: Conservative (default: quantization off) and Optimized (profile enabled with 1% quality SLA; pricing reflects committed usage).
- Private: provide artifacts and validated profiles; charge a packaging fee + support for updates.
- Discount framing: present estimated savings and a recommended profile per-model to customers based on their historical sequence length distribution.

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Edge-case quality regressions for niche prompt patterns. Mitigation: enlarge canonical prompt-sets and require human review for domain-critical tenants before Dedicated expansion.
- Risk: Billing disputes due to per-profile metering. Mitigation: expose per-profile metering exports and reconciliation reports.
- Risk: Runtime incompatibilities across older hardware. Mitigation: compatibility matrix in Profile Registry and automatic routing to base variant when no compatible kernels exist.

Timeline and milestones (quarter-level):
- Week 0–4: Profile Registry + Prompt-set authoring + Billing schema changes.
- Week 5–6: Internal canary + human rater batch.
- Week 7–10: External controlled canary.
- Week 11–16: Staged expansion and Dedicated customer onboarding.
- Week 17–18: GA, docs, and billing live.

Appendices:
A) Example billing multiplier table:
| profile_name | quant_bits | estimated_token_cost_multiplier | notes |
| q4_small | 4 | 0.70 | Best for short sequences, slight bias observed on numeric tasks |
| q8_dynamic | 8 | 0.85 | Low risk, moderate savings |
| q4_tf_robust | 4 | 0.65 | Requires special kernel; higher memory savings |

B) Example automated eval config (YAML):
--
prompt_set_ids: ["safety_v1", "hallucination_basic_v2", "finance_smoke_v1"]
metrics:
  - name: normalized_utility
    threshold: 0.985   # allow 1.5% drop
  - name: hallucination_rate
    threshold: 0.02
retries: 3
backfill_days: 7
--

C) Rollout decision checklist (to move from canary to staged):
1) Automated metrics pass for 14 consecutive days.
2) Human rater sample error <= target.
3) No billing inconsistencies in reconciliation report.
4) No more than one unrelated SRE incident correlated to profile.

Next steps (action items):
- Product: finalize profile taxonomy and UI copy (owner: Maya) — due 2026-11-22.
- Runtime: implement profile_id tagging and fallback plumbing (owner: Rafael) — due 2026-11-29.
- Evals: curate initial prompt-sets and schedule human rater batch (owner: Priya) — due 2026-11-26.
- Billing: update metering schema and export (owner: Aisha) — due 2026-11-30.
